answer: Marginal-cost identity ladder. Each new identity pays a fee equal to the prior one's squared, so an attacker's tenth identity costs 100x the first—arity becomes the attacker's own bill. A cheap echo of a single identity cannot scale without the curve steepening against it. The enforcement rule: registration price rises with each identity tied to the same funding thread. Attackers who mint thousands pay a superlinear sum; honest users paying once stay near the floor. Any fable of cheap sybils dies at the arithmetic.
